subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should maintainers keep this umbrella open while splitting the Windows gateway-down modes into narrower tracked fixes, or close it in favor of existing narrower Windows restart issues?
rationale: The issue combines confirmed source gaps with live-only Windows failure modes and overlapping open PRs, so automation should not choose the product split, priority order, or umbrella ownership by itself.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open as the tracking umbrella, promote separate owner-reviewed fixes for idempotent startup, invalid-config repair, browser isolation, and pricing readiness, and close subitems as they land with live Windows proof.

options.title: Route entirely to existing narrower issues
options.body: Close this umbrella only if maintainers decide the existing Windows restart and browser/config issues fully cover every reported failure mode and can absorb the reporter evidence.

options.title: Wait for live repro before splitting
options.body: Hold the umbrella open with no implementation work until a maintainer or trusted Windows run reproduces the Edge crash, orphaned processes, and pricing readiness stalls on current main.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the tracking umbrella, promote separate owner-reviewed fixes for idempotent startup, invalid-config repair, browser isolation, and pricing readiness, and close subitems as they land with live Windows proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main gateway/browser/runtime hardening makes this the best available coordinator for splitting the umbrella across owners.
